gloss: retirement from active life; retired person

definitions.gloss: retirement from active life; living in seclusion
definitions.explanation: Withdrawing from work or public life to live quietly. Historically, referred to a family head formally transferring authority to a successor and stepping back from active duties.
A person who has retired from active life. Can be used playfully or self-deprecatingly to describe someone living a quiet, unhurried lifestyle.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{六十歳|ろくじっさい}で{隠居|いんきょ}した。
{隠居|いんきょ}{生活|せいかつ}を{楽|たの}しんでいる。
{店|みせ}を{息子|むすこ}に{任|まか}せて{隠居|いんきょ}するつもりだ。
examples.english: I plan to hand the shop over to my son and retire.

examples.japanese: {隣|となり}の{隠居|いんきょ}さんは{将棋|しょうぎ}が{強|つよ}い。
examples.english: The retired old man next door is good at shogi.

examples.japanese: まだ{若|わか}いのに{隠居|いんきょ}みたいな{生活|せいかつ}をしている。
examples.english: Even though you're still young, you're living like a retiree.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きな{屋敷|やしき}の{離|はな}れに{隠居|いんきょ}が{暮|く}らしていた。
examples.english: A retired elder lived in the annex of the large mansion.

notes:
Compound of {隠|いん} (to hide) + {居|きょ} (to reside). Originally a feudal-era practice where a household head formally stepped down.

SENSE 1 (retirement):
In the Edo period, {隠居|いんきょ} was a formal legal act where the head of a family transferred authority to an heir. Today it is used more loosely for any retirement from active professional life.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (sense 1):
- {隠居|いんきょ}する (to retire)
- {隠居|いんきょ}{生活|せいかつ} (retired life)

SENSE 2 (retired person):
Can refer to a retired elder or be used humorously about someone living a very quiet, inactive lifestyle.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (sense 2):
- {隠居|いんきょ}さん (the retired old person — affectionate)
- {隠居|いんきょ}{暮|ぐ}らし (a retiree's lifestyle)
